body: @annevk  Any thoughts on this?

This addresses #1897 and #3077 though @smaug---- had some concerns in the former. I'm not sure if he still believes we should leave `contenteditable` behind. That still doesn't seem like a good solution to me.

How do https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=28228 and https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=28747 fit into this data model? Would they be fully independent?

Did you intentionally rename the IDL attribute? They normally use camelcase.

We also need to mention this attribute in the list of global attributes.
(I wonder if we should also define that certain `pattern` attribute values as per https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1626#issuecomment-332501219 end up selecting an input mode.)
As I said during TPAC, I've given up the hope that we'll have a non-broken contentEditable ever, so adding more stuff there is, I guess, ok.
cc @jessi3py
@dtapuska for clarity, I'm awaiting your thoughts on my initial feedback before doing a more detailed review.
It would also be good to get @whatwg/a11y and @whatwg/i18n to weigh in here now we're substantially altering the feature.

@dtapuska to be clear, the IDL attribute needs to use camelcase (and is case-sensitive in usage), the content attribute needs to remain lowercase (that one is case-insensitive).

As for `pattern`; certain strings trigger a different input mode. Probably that is done by just comparing strings though and not actually parsing and figuring something out from the resulting structure.

WebKit has long had this bug:
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=23588

For Firefox which implements the current spec (behind a feature flag) I've opened this bug:
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1424284

Opened bug against Edge:
https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/platform/issues/15018728/

The i18n WG briefly discussed this yesterday afternoon, and one further potential issue was brought up.  

>  The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of numeric input. Keys 0-9 should be shown. This keyword is useful for PIN entry. 

We suspect that this may need some finessing for locales where local number digits are used (such as Thai, Hindi, Arabic. etc.).  If the `numeric` keyword really means `pin` or something similar, perhaps it should be called that?  (I don't know whether pin numbers for users who speak those languages require use of the 0-9 keys or not.)

The `decimal` keyword is likely to be more problematic, since we assume that users will expect to type decimal numbers in their local digits.

@r12a  These are intended to be mappings onto native OS controls such as: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/widget/TextView.html#attr_android:inputType

It does not inhibit the keyboard presenting something for local digits. I should then probably remove the Keys 0-9 from the text and make no reference to that.

> I should then probably remove the Keys 0-9 from the text and make no reference to that.

Yes, i think that's what we were thinking of, in addition to just running a quick sense-check to ensure that there's nothing blocking that.
@domenic I don't think there are any implementations of `inputmode`. So I think we actually need agreement on that.

@smaug---- @jessi3py is Gecko interested in the changes in this PR? That would amount to (a) unflagging inputmode; (b) removing any support you had for the old input modes (e.g. katakana); (c) supporting inputmode on contenteditable elements too.

I don't know what (a) means.
Why removing support for the old stuff is related to this?
And (c) makes sense then.

My understanding is that Gecko implements the current spec behind a feature flag, so I was wondering what that means for this feature in general and whether there were any plans to unflag it.

Removing support for old stuff was also done in this PR, narrowing it down only to ones implementable in current virtual keyboard implementations. I'm not sure if Gecko somehow implemented those, but we wanted to check if Gecko supported that removal.

Seeking clarification: https://whatpr.org/html/3260/ede1de1...6048676/interaction.html#input-modalities:-the-inputmode-attribute says "The user agent should display a virtual keyboard..."

Is it the user agent or the system that displays the keyboard? I'm happy to be corrected, but i expected it to say something like "The user agent prompts the system or device to display a virtual keyboard...".

Also, minor typo in decimal: 'seperator' -> 'separator'.

I don't think making that distinction is something we want to do. In general we don't talk about anything under the user agent level, and leave how or whether it reuses the underlying OS's mechanisms as an implementation detail.
I agree with @domenic. For example on ChromeOS the architecture is such that the UA displays the virtual keyboard but going into those details shouldn't be relevant in the spec.
@smaug----  I believe a) is referring to that inputmode is still behind a preferences flag.

Firefox's implementation was added in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=746142 and does not appear to be behind a flag and also appears to be out-of-line with the current HTML Standard. I suspect this was added for FxOS and has since been forgotten about. The warning from @smaug---- about keeping up with any eventual HTML Standard was also forgotten about. It's probably not worth worrying much about.
